sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九的隐形。,

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗马·马斯。,

sentences.en: I fell in love with architecture on the Chicago River.
sentences.zh: 我是在芝加哥河畔爱上建筑的。,

sentences.en: You can endlessly argue about which city has the greatest architecture,
sentences.zh: 你可以无休止地争论哪个城市拥有最伟大的建筑，,

sentences.en: but one thing that puts Chicago near the top for me
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，让芝加哥名列前茅的一个重要原因,

sentences.en: is that the Chicago River provides a beautiful vantage point
sentences.zh: 是芝加哥河提供了一个绝佳的视角，,

sentences.en: to take in all the marvelous skyscrapers.
sentences.zh: 让人能够饱览所有美妙的摩天大楼。,

sentences.en: Rather than being crammed in on the sidewalk between looming towers,
sentences.zh: 比起挤在耸立的高楼之间的人行道上，,

sentences.en: trying and probably failing to take it all in,
sentences.zh: 试图却可能无法将一切尽收眼底，,

sentences.en: the river pushes the buildings apart
sentences.zh: 河流把建筑物隔开，,

sentences.en: and gives you the opportunity to coast by on the roof of a ferry
sentences.zh: 让你有机会乘坐渡轮的顶层甲板顺流而下，,

sentences.en: with glass, steel, and concrete wonders
sentences.zh: 四周环绕着玻璃、钢铁和混凝土的奇迹，,

sentences.en: presented in their full glory everywhere you turn.
sentences.zh: 无论你转向哪里，它们都以最壮丽的姿态呈现在眼前。,

sentences.en: But probably the city's biggest design achievement isn't a building at all.
sentences.zh: 但这座城市最伟大的设计成就可能根本不是某座建筑。,

sentences.en: It's that river itself,
sentences.zh: 而是这条河本身，,

sentences.en: a waterway disguised as a remnant of the natural landscape.
sentences.zh: 一条伪装成自然景观遗迹的水道。,

sentences.en: But it really isn't.
sentences.zh: 但它其实并不是。,

sentences.en: It's hard to tell when you see the river, but it's going the wrong way.
sentences.zh: 当你看到这条河时很难察觉，但它的流向是反的。,

sentences.en: It should flow into Lake Michigan.
sentences.zh: 它本该流入密歇根湖。,

sentences.en: But instead, fresh water from Lake Michigan flows backwards into the city.
sentences.zh: 但相反，密歇根湖的淡水却倒流进了城市。,

sentences.en: The Chicago River is, in a large part,
sentences.zh: 芝加哥河在很大程度上，,

sentences.en: a carefully designed extension of the city's sewer system.
sentences.zh: 是这座城市下水道系统经过精心设计的延伸。,

sentences.en: Even calling it a river may be off base.
sentences.zh: 甚至叫它河流可能都不太恰当。,

sentences.en: It's not really a river.
sentences.zh: 它其实并不是一条河。,

sentences.en: In Chicago, it's really the Chicago Canal.
sentences.zh: 在芝加哥，它实际上是芝加哥运河。,

sentences.en: There's not an inch, I don't think, of the Chicago River
sentences.zh: 我认为芝加哥河没有哪怕一英寸，,

sentences.en: that is natural in Chicago.
sentences.zh: 在芝加哥是天然的。,

sentences.en: That's Richard Cahan.
sentences.zh: 那是理查德·卡汉。,

sentences.en: He's a journalist and historian in Chicago.
sentences.zh: 他是芝加哥的一名记者和历史学家。,

sentences.en: And in 2012, he co-wrote and published a book called
sentences.zh: 在2012年，他参与合著并出版了一本书，名叫,

sentences.en: The Lost Panoramas,
sentences.zh: 《失落的全景》，,

sentences.en: when Chicago changed its river and the land beyond.
sentences.zh: 讲述芝加哥如何改变其河流以及远处的土地。,

sentences.en: And it's filled with these gorgeous pictures from before
sentences.zh: 书中充满了这些华丽的照片，记录了前后的变化，,

sentences.en: and mostly after one of the biggest urban design projects ever,
sentences.zh: 尤其是史上最大规模的城市设计项目之一之后，,

sentences.en: the reversal and the complete transformation of the Chicago River.
sentences.zh: 即芝加哥河的逆流工程与彻底改造。,

sentences.en: And that is Dan Weissman, a journalist, lover of triangular buildings,
sentences.zh: 那是丹·韦斯曼，一名记者、三角形建筑爱好者，,

sentences.en: and a lifelong, die-hard Chicagoan.
sentences.zh: 以及土生土长的坚定芝加哥人。,

sentences.en: And reversing the river was actually the third in the series of epic design projects
sentences.zh: 而河流逆流其实是一系列史诗级设计项目中的第三个，,

sentences.en: spanning almost 50 years.
sentences.zh: 跨度将近50年。,

sentences.en: Three projects that amounted to 19th century engineers
sentences.zh: 这三个项目相当于19世纪的工程师们，,

sentences.en: just taking it to the laws of nature,
sentences.zh: 公然向自然规律叫板，,

sentences.en: with a kind of moxie that just seems to be folded into the DNA of 19th century engineers.
sentences.zh: 带着一种仿佛已经融入19世纪工程师DNA的冲劲。,

sentences.en: And with just the first two,
sentences.zh: 仅仅通过前两个项目，,

sentences.en: we're talking about two decades of massive, ridiculous achievements.
sentences.zh: 我们就谈论了长达二十年的宏大而离谱的成就。,

sentences.en: Stuff that changed people's ideas of how far you could go to make a city work.
sentences.zh: 这些东西改变了人们对为了让城市运转到底能走多远的看法。,

sentences.en: And those two have been so obscured by time
sentences.zh: 而前两个项目已经被时间严重湮没，,

sentences.en: that the dude who did them,
sentences.zh: 以至于那个完成这些成就的家伙——,

sentences.en: and yet it was basically one guy who proposed and executed
sentences.zh: 基本上就是一个提出并执行了,

sentences.en: not one, but two of these incredible projects.
sentences.zh: 不仅一个、而是两个如此不可思议的项目的人——,

sentences.en: He's basically unknown today.
sentences.zh: 如今几乎鲜为人知。,

sentences.en: Ellis Chesbrough.
sentences.zh: 埃利斯·切斯布罗。,

sentences.en: If you've never heard of Ellis Chesbrough, you're not alone.
sentences.zh: 如果你从未听说过埃利斯·切斯布罗，你并不孤单。,

sentences.en: In fact, as I record this, he doesn't even have a Wikipedia entry.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在我录音时，他甚至连维基百科词条都没有。,

sentences.en: But you can bet Richard Cahan knows who he is.
sentences.zh: 但你可以确信理查德·卡汉知道他是谁。,

sentences.en: So he was a star, and his house is just north of downtown,
sentences.zh: 所以他曾是个大人物，他的房子就在市中心以北，,

sentences.en: and there's a little plaque in front of the house.
sentences.zh: 房子前面有一块小牌匾。,

sentences.en: I once parked my car in front of it.
sentences.zh: 我曾经把车停在它前面。,

sentences.en: Always read the plaque.
sentences.zh: 一定要读读牌匾。,

sentences.en: And it says, House of Ellis Chesbrough,
sentences.zh: 上面写着：埃利斯·切斯布罗故居，,

sentences.en: and I'm sure I'm the only person that ever was very excited about seeing it.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定我是唯一一个看到它会如此兴奋的人。,

sentences.en: Oh, but back in the 1800s, Chesbrough was the man.
sentences.zh: 哦，但在19世纪，切斯布罗可是个大红人。,

sentences.en: And no one has ever worked harder to save Chicago from its own poop.
sentences.zh: 从来没有人像他那样努力把芝加哥从它自己的粪便中拯救出来。,

sentences.en: Poop.
sentences.zh: 粪便。,

sentences.en: The thing that has brought cities to their knees for millennia.
sentences.zh: 几千年来一直让各大城市陷入困境的东西。,

sentences.en: Now here's the setup.
sentences.zh: 现在背景是这样的。,

sentences.en: The city of Chicago had been growing like crazy for a couple of decades out of nothing.
sentences.zh: 芝加哥这座城市在短短几十年里从无到有，疯狂发展。,

sentences.en: Huge boomtown, more than doubling its population every few years.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的新兴城市，每隔几年人口就会翻一番以上。,

sentences.en: And then wham, cholera epidemic wiped out 6% of the city.
sentences.zh: 然后砰的一声，霍乱疫情夺去了这座城市6%的人口。,

sentences.en: That summer, one account had cholera killing 60 people a day in a town of 70,000.
sentences.zh: 那个夏天，据记载，在一个7万人口的小镇里，霍乱每天夺走60人的生命。,

sentences.en: One observer put it this way.
sentences.zh: 一位目击者是这样描述的。,

sentences.en: The death cart was constantly in the street.
sentences.zh: 运尸车源源不断地在街上驶过。,

sentences.en: And not to be gross, but cholera, it is a super nasty way to go.
sentences.zh: 虽然听起来可能有点恶心，但霍乱死法极其痛苦难堪。,

sentences.en: It's sudden, painful, and, well, gross.
sentences.zh: 它来得突然、痛苦，而且，嗯，恶心。,

sentences.en: Vomiting, diarrhea, horrible cramps.
sentences.zh: 呕吐、腹泻、可怕的痉挛。,

sentences.en: You're dead in less than a day, but it is a really, really unpleasant day.
sentences.zh: 不到一天你就会丧命，但这绝对是极其极其难熬的一天。,

sentences.en: So people were freaking out.
sentences.zh: 所以人们都吓坏了。,

sentences.en: Enter Chesbrough, who made a name with work he'd done in Boston.
sentences.zh: 切斯布罗登场了，他在波士顿的工作中声名鹊起。,

sentences.en: What you people need, he told Chicago, is a sewer system,
sentences.zh: 你们这些人需要的是一个下水道系统，他告诉芝加哥人，,

sentences.en: which was actually a newish idea at the time in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这在当时的美国其实是个相当新的概念。,

sentences.en: No other city here had one.
sentences.zh: 这里的其他城市都没有。,

sentences.en: Sewers, yes.
sentences.zh: 下水道是有的，,

sentences.en: Systems, not so much.
sentences.zh: 但系统化的就没有了。,

sentences.en: And Chicago didn't seem like the town you'd pick to go firSt.
sentences.zh: 芝加哥看起来并不像是你会选作第一个吃螃蟹的城镇。,

sentences.en: Not if you thought topography meant anything.
sentences.zh: 除非你认为地形有什么意义的话。,

sentences.en: I mean, Chicago was built on a swamp.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，芝加哥是建立在沼泽上的。,

sentences.en: Street level?
sentences.zh: 街道高度？,

sentences.en: Water level?
sentences.zh: 水位高度？,

sentences.en: Pretty much the same thing.
sentences.zh: 几乎是一回事。,

sentences.en: So you put sewers under the street,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你把下水道建在街道下面，,

sentences.en: there's no way for the material in them to, you know, run downhill into anything.
sentences.zh: 里面的东西根本没法靠重力向下流淌到任何地方。,

sentences.en: So here it comes, round one.
sentences.zh: 所以，第一回合来了。,

sentences.en: The first of these three projects that proved Chicago was ready to try anything.
sentences.zh: 这三个项目中证明芝加哥准备尝试任何事物的第一个项目。,

sentences.en: Chesbrough said, okay, let's jack street level up 10 feet.
sentences.zh: 切斯布罗说，好吧，让我们把街道高度抬高10英尺。,

sentences.en: It was a time when engineers were really seen as the saviors.
sentences.zh: 那是一个工程师被真正视为救世主的时代。,

sentences.en: And so when he said, first off, that we're going to build a sewer system,
sentences.zh: 因此，当他首先说我们要建造一个下水道系统，,

sentences.en: and he said we're going to raise Chicago up 10 feet so that we can put in sewers,
sentences.zh: 并且说我们要把芝加哥垫高10英尺以便安装下水道时，,

sentences.en: everyone in Chicago says, great, great idea, let's do it.
sentences.zh: 芝加哥的每个人都说，太棒了，好主意，我们干吧。,

sentences.en: Yeah, and there was a reason they went for it.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们这么做是有原因的。,

sentences.en: People were making tons of money.
sentences.zh: 人们在赚大钱。,

sentences.en: Chicago's location was perfect, connecting the west to the east through railroads in the Great Lakes.
sentences.zh: 芝加哥的地理位置完美，通过铁路和五大湖将西部与东部连接起来。,

sentences.en: And that's why the city was growing so fast to start with.
sentences.zh: 这就是这座城市一开始发展如此之快的原因。,

sentences.en: Actually, they didn't jack up the streets themselves.
sentences.zh: 其实，他们并没有把街道本身撬起来。,

sentences.en: They just piled dirt on top of the old streets to make them higher.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在旧街道上堆土把它们垫高。,

sentences.en: And some of that dirt came from the river bottom,
sentences.zh: 其中一些泥土来自河底，,

sentences.en: which they had dredged to make room for all of the stuff that they were about to dump in there.
sentences.zh: 他们为了给即将倾倒进去的大量杂物腾出空间而对河底进行了疏浚。,

sentences.en: But they did jack up the buildings.
sentences.zh: 但他们确实把建筑物给顶起来了。,

sentences.en: Literally, they put the buildings on jack screws, a lot of jack screws, and started cranking.
sentences.zh: 字面意思，他们把建筑物放在千斤顶上，很多很多千斤顶，然后开始摇动。,

sentences.en: There's this great picture from 1857.
sentences.zh: 有一张1857年的绝妙照片。,

sentences.en: It shows a massive hotel, big as a city block, at least three or four stories tall,
sentences.zh: 它显示了一座巨大的酒店，大得像一个城市街区，至少有三四层楼高，,

sentences.en: with dozens and dozens of guys cranking away in perfect sync.
sentences.zh: 有几十个人正以完美的同步节奏摇动着千斤顶。,

sentences.en: Ready, men?
sentences.zh: 准备好了吗，伙计们？,

sentences.en: Turn!
You can also see hotel guests in top hats standing on the balconies a couple flights up.
sentences.zh: 你还可以看到戴着高顶礼帽的酒店客人在几层楼高的阳台上站着。,

sentences.en: They're looking out, watching their view get better and better, a quarter inch at a time.
sentences.zh: 他们向外眺望，看着自己的视野一点一点变得越来越好，每次四分之一英寸。,

sentences.en: And this kind of thing happened over and over again,
sentences.zh: 这种事情一次又一次地发生，,

sentences.en: with businesses staying open while they were getting cranked up, just for kicks.
sentences.zh: 企业在被顶升的同时照常营业，纯粹是为了好玩。,

sentences.en: Another fancy hotel had 1,200 guys cranking away all at once.
sentences.zh: 另一家豪华酒店有1200名工人同时在摇动千斤顶。,

sentences.en: Meanwhile, apparently there were teams of masons laying bricks for a new foundation at top speed,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，显然有一队队的泥瓦匠在全速为新地基砌砖，,

sentences.en: literally working around the guys with the jack screws.
sentences.zh: 简直就是在操作千斤顶的工人身边争分夺秒地工作。,

sentences.en: There's another great picture of a huge downtown block of stores and offices getting hoisted up.
sentences.zh: 还有另一张精彩的照片，展示了市中心一大片商店和办公室街区被整体吊起。,

sentences.en: All 35,000 tons of it.
sentences.zh: 足足有35000吨重。,

sentences.en: Jacking up the streets and buildings took like 20 years to finish.
sentences.zh: 抬高街道和建筑物花了大约20年才完成。,

sentences.en: But by that time, project number two was already done.
sentences.zh: 但到那时，第二个项目已经完成了。,

sentences.en: Because it didn't take too long after the sewers went in
sentences.zh: 因为下水道投入使用后没多久，,

sentences.en: for Chicago to realize that there was a big question
sentences.zh: 芝加哥人就意识到有一个重大问题，,

sentences.en: that they hadn't given enough thought to on the first go-round.
sentences.zh: 他们在第一轮中没有给予足够的重视。,

sentences.en: Where did the sewers take all this output?
sentences.zh: 下水道把所有这些排泄物都带到了哪里？,

sentences.en: Into the river.
sentences.zh: 流进了河里。,

sentences.en: And where'd the river go?
sentences.zh: 那河流流向哪里？,

sentences.en: Into the lake.
sentences.zh: 流进了湖里。,

sentences.en: And where was the drinking water coming from?
sentences.zh: 饮用水又是从哪里来的？,

sentences.en: Oops.
sentences.zh: 糟糕。,

sentences.en: So okay, said Chesbro, how about this?
sentences.zh: 好吧，切斯布罗说，这样如何？,

sentences.en: We'll build water intakes two miles out from shore,
sentences.zh: 我们在离海岸两英里的地方建造取水口，,

sentences.en: way past where the river dumps our muck into the lake.
sentences.zh: 远远超出河流将污物倾倒进湖里的地方。,

sentences.en: And that'll mean digging the biggest, deepest, longest tunnel ever up to this point.
sentences.zh: 这意味着要开挖迄今为止最大、最深、最长的隧道。,

sentences.en: What do you think?
sentences.zh: 你们觉得怎么样？,

sentences.en: They all said fine, and they did it, and it was amazing.
sentences.zh: 大家都说好，于是他们照做了，这太惊人了。,

sentences.en: Again, the city is growing, people are making money, and everybody agrees.
sentences.zh: 城市再次发展，人们在赚钱，每个人都表示赞同。,

sentences.en: They'll do whatever it takes to keep this thing rolling.
sentences.zh: 他们会不惜一切代价让这一切继续运转。,

sentences.en: So it's on round two, digging the tunnels.
sentences.zh: 于是进入第二回合，开挖隧道。,

sentences.en: In 1864, Chesbro's guys start digging the tunnel out from the city, 60 feet down from street level.
sentences.zh: 1864年，切斯布罗的手下开始从市中心向外开挖隧道，距离街面60英尺深。,

sentences.en: A year after that, they install a giant structure two miles out in the lake.
sentences.zh: 一年后，他们在湖中两英里处安装了一个巨大的结构。,

sentences.en: They call them cribs.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为进水井楼（cribs）。,

sentences.en: And start digging a tunnel in from under that, back towards shore.
sentences.zh: 并开始从那里下方开挖隧道，向海岸方向推进。,

sentences.en: The work went on around the clock, from both sides.
sentences.zh: 这项工作日夜不停地从两端同时进行。,

sentences.en: One crew dug by hand for 16 hours a day.
sentences.zh: 一个施工队每天手工挖掘16个小时。,

sentences.en: Then a crew of bricklayers took the graveyard shift, shoring up the area that had just been dug out.
sentences.zh: 然后一队泥瓦匠接上夜班，加固刚刚挖出来的区域。

sentences.en: In November 1865, the two sets of crews met in the middle, just about dead on centered.
sentences.zh: 1865年11月，两支施工队在中间会合，位置基本上精准居中。

sentences.en: Needless to say, this is before GPS.
sentences.zh: 不用说，这是在GPS发明之前。

sentences.en: You know, this is just all by sight.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这全凭肉眼观察。

sentences.en: Everybody agreed.
sentences.zh: 大家都表示赞同。

sentences.en: Chesbro was a genius and a half.
sentences.zh: 切斯布罗绝对是个绝顶天才。

sentences.en: Except they hadn't really solved the problem.
sentences.zh: 只不过问题并没有真正解决。

sentences.en: The city was still growing like crazy.
sentences.zh: 这座城市依然在疯狂扩张。

sentences.en: Maybe 200,000 people by 1865.
sentences.zh: 到1865年，人口可能已经达到了20万。

sentences.en: And they were dumping more of their business into the river than ever, which stank.
sentences.zh: 而且他们排进河里的商业废水比以往任何时候都多，臭气熏天。

sentences.en: And before the water from the new intakes even started flowing, the Union Stockyards opened on the river's south branch and upped the ante.
sentences.zh: 就在新的进水口开始供水之前，联合屠宰场在河流的南支开业了，这直接加大了赌注。

sentences.en: We're talking 320 acres of slaughterhouses and meatpacking plants, all of them, dumping whatever they couldn't use.
sentences.zh: 我们说的是占地320英亩的屠宰场和肉类加工厂，它们把所有无法利用的东西全都倒进河里。

sentences.en: And just imagine what that would be into the river.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象一下，这倒进河里会是什么情景。

sentences.en: Well, they estimated that the stockyards were the equivalent of a million people's discharges.
sentences.zh: 好吧，据估计，这些屠宰场的排污量相当于一百万人口的排放量。

sentences.en: And there weren't even a million people in the city then.
sentences.zh: 当时城里甚至还没有一百万人。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's true.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: That bit of the south fork still goes by the name it got then, Bubbly Creek.
sentences.zh: 南支流的那一小段至今仍沿用当年的名字，叫泡泡溪。

sentences.en: All the discarded animal stuff would rot at the bottom of the river and eventually give off methane, which would bubble up to the surface and burSt.
sentences.zh: 所有丢弃的动物废料会在河底腐烂，最终产生甲烷，甲烷会冒泡浮到水面上并破裂。

sentences.en: Also, sometimes it caught fire.
sentences.zh: 此外，有时候它还会着火。

sentences.en: And sometimes the sewage got swept more than two miles out and fouled the water intakes.
sentences.zh: 有时污水甚至会被冲到两英里以外，污染取水口。

sentences.en: Later, they dig these even further out.
sentences.zh: 后来，他们把取水口挖得更远。

sentences.en: There's one called the Four Mile Crib.
sentences.zh: 有一个叫四英里 crib 的地方。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, the city kept growing.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，这座城市仍在继续发展。

sentences.en: By 1880, we're talking half a million people and producing more excrement.
sentences.zh: 到了1880年，人口已经达到五十万，产生的排泄物也更多了。

sentences.en: The stockyards grew too.
sentences.zh: 屠宰场也在扩张。

sentences.en: A lot.
sentences.zh: 规模很大。

sentences.en: One engineer would say, Chicago produces more filth per capita than any other city.
sentences.zh: 曾有一位工程师说过，芝加哥人均产生的污秽比其他任何城市都多。

sentences.en: And now typhoid was getting to be a problem.
sentences.zh: 而现在，伤寒也开始成为一个问题。

sentences.en: So Chicago started pushing for a new state law to help undertake the biggest, baddest, craziest idea ever.
sentences.zh: 因此，芝加哥开始推动一项新的州法律，以着手实施有史以来最大、最狠、最疯狂的想法。

sentences.en: They decided to dig a gigantic new canal that would reverse the river entirely.
sentences.zh: 他们决定开挖一条崭新的巨型运河，彻底逆转这条河流的流向。

sentences.en: Reversing the river would bring in fresh water from the lake and keep Chicago's muck from polluting the drinking water pulled from that same lake.
sentences.zh: 逆转河流可以将湖泊的淡水引入，并防止芝加哥的污泥污染从同一个湖泊中提取的饮用水。

sentences.en: And flush all the sewage down to the Illinois River, which would then take it out to the Mississippi.
sentences.zh: 并将所有污水冲入伊利诺伊河，然后再由其排入密西西比河。

sentences.en: It took a few years to get the new law approved.
sentences.zh: 新法律的批准花了几年时间。

sentences.en: The town of Joliet saw a river of crap coming its way and tried to nix it.
sentences.zh: 乔利埃特镇看到滚滚粪河向自己涌来，便试图阻止。

sentences.en: And then it took a few more years to get plans laid out and contracts issued.
sentences.zh: 接着又花了几年时间来制定规划和下达合同。

sentences.en: And then it was shovel day.
sentences.zh: 然后就迎来了动工日。

sentences.en: September 3rd, 1892.
More than a thousand people came out to watch.
sentences.zh: 一千多名观众赶来观看。

sentences.en: An official took one cut with a nickel-plated shovel.
sentences.zh: 一位官员用一把镀镍的铲子铲下了第一铲。

sentences.en: And then an engineer detonated two massive loads of dynamite.
sentences.zh: 随后，一名工程师引爆了两大堆炸药。

sentences.en: Dynamite was their preferred weapon against the environment.
sentences.zh: 炸药是他们对抗环境的首选武器。

sentences.en: And it was on, round three, in the epic struggle against Chicago's own excreta, reversing the river.
sentences.zh: 好戏开场了，这是在与芝加哥自身的排泄物进行史诗般斗争的第三轮，逆转河流。

sentences.en: 28 miles of canal.
sentences.zh: 28英里长的运河。

sentences.en: Price tag, $31 million and change.
sentences.zh: 造价3100万美元零一点。

sentences.en: In today's money, almost $23 billion.
sentences.zh: 折合今天的货币，将近230亿美元。

sentences.en: As many as 8,700 guys working at a time, with work going on year-round.
sentences.zh: 同时有多达8700名工人进行全年无休的施工。

sentences.en: Tons and tons of dynamite.
sentences.zh: 数以吨计的炸药。

sentences.en: You could hear the blasts downtown when the wind was right.
sentences.zh: 风向合适时，在市中心就能听到爆炸声。

sentences.en: And enormous machines.
sentences.zh: 还有巨大的机械。

sentences.en: Some invented special for the project, including a 640-foot-wide monster conveyor, which broke after less than a year.
sentences.zh: 有些是专门为该项目发明的，包括一个640英尺宽的巨型输送机，使用不到一年就坏了。

sentences.en: But still.
sentences.zh: 不过话虽如此。

sentences.en: During the 1893 World's Fair, tourists by the thousands day-tripped out to the construction zone.
sentences.zh: 在1893年芝加哥世博会期间，成千上万的游客一日游来到施工区。

sentences.en: They would take boats and trains out to the site to see the work.
sentences.zh: 他们会乘船和火车前往现场参观施工。

sentences.en: And people were coming to Chicago, and they were like, you gotta see this.
sentences.zh: 人们来到芝加哥，都会说，你一定要来看看这个。

sentences.en: You know, this town is amazing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这座城镇太神奇了。

sentences.en: And they'll do anything to survive.
sentences.zh: 为了生存他们什么都干得出来。

sentences.en: Even after the fair closed, train companies ran morning specials so local sightseers could check out the big machines and those ever-popular dynamite blasts.
sentences.zh: 即使在世博会闭幕后，铁路公司仍开通了早间专列，以便当地游客参观大型机械和那些备受欢迎的炸药爆破。

sentences.en: This was an amazing project.
sentences.zh: 这是一个了不起的项目。

sentences.en: You know, so many people know about the Panama Canal, but it was really in building this canal that they figured out everything engineering-wise and the equipment.
sentences.zh: 你知道，很多人都知道巴拿马运河，但实际上正是在建造这条运河的过程中，他们在工程学和设备方面摸索出了一切。

sentences.en: And a lot of the engineers went to Panama.
sentences.zh: 许多工程师后来都去了巴拿马。

sentences.en: And then, very late in the game, St. Louis got pissed.
sentences.zh: 然后，在项目快要结束的时候，圣路易斯生气了。

sentences.en: We're talking 1899.
sentences.zh: 我们说的是1899年。

sentences.en: All the major digging has been done for years.
sentences.zh: 所有的大规模挖掘工作多年来已经完成。

sentences.en: And the fine-tuning stuff is getting wrapped up.
sentences.zh: 微调的工作也即将收尾。

sentences.en: All the construction of bridges, some extra digging in the rivers downstream that are going to carry Chicago's water toward the Mississippi and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 所有桥梁的建设，以及下游河流中一些用于将芝加哥的水运往密西西比河等地的额外挖掘工作。

sentences.en: And that stuff is very, very close to finished.
sentences.zh: 这些工作已经非常非常接近完成。

sentences.en: And this is when St. Louis figures out that all that water, carrying who knows what, is headed down the Mississippi upriver of St. Louis,
sentences.zh: 正是在这个时候，圣路易斯发现所有这些夹杂着不明物体的水正沿着密西西比河朝着圣路易斯上游流去，

sentences.en: which depends on the river for its drinking water and for brewing Budweiser beer.
sentences.zh: 而圣路易斯正依赖这条河获得饮用水和酿造百威啤酒。

sentences.en: The city authorizes its attorney to prepare a lawsuit asking the U.S.
sentences.zh: 该市授权其律师准备起诉，向美国

sentences.en: Supreme Court for an injunction that would stop the sanitary district of Chicago from opening up the dams and letting that water go.
sentences.zh: 最高法院申请禁令，阻止芝加哥卫生局打开水坝放水。

sentences.en: Thing is, it takes a while to get a lawsuit ready, a few months, say.
sentences.zh: 问题是，准备诉讼需要一段时间，比方说几个月。

sentences.en: And Chicago starts humping it to get the dams ready to open before St. Louis can get an injunction.
sentences.zh: 于是芝加哥开始加紧干活，赶在圣路易斯申请禁令之前把水坝准备好并打开。

sentences.en: So, New Year's Day, 1900.
sentences.zh: 就这样，1900年元旦到了。

sentences.en: The sanitary district trustees decide the major work is done.
sentences.zh: 卫生局理事们认为主要工作已经完成。

sentences.en: The next day, January 2, they head out to a spot on the city's southwest side where there's this one little temporary dam holding back the river
sentences.zh: 第二天，即1月2日，他们前往市西南部的一个地点，那里有一座临时小水坝挡住了河水，

sentences.en: from this massive 28-mile canal that's waiting for all that water.
sentences.zh: 防止水流入这条等待蓄水的28英里长的巨大运河。

sentences.en: However, the trustees arrive at dawn.
sentences.zh: 然而，理事们在黎明时分到达。

sentences.en: One of them brings shovels.
sentences.zh: 其中一人带了铲子。

sentences.en: Most of these projects have these beautiful gold shovels, but one of the trustees just stopped at a hardware store and bought these kind of tinny old, you know, work shovels.
sentences.zh: 大多数这类工程都有漂亮的纯金铁锹，但其中一位理事只是在五金店顺便买了几把那种劣质的、旧的、你知道的工作铁锹。

sentences.en: It's like stopping at Home Depot.
sentences.zh: 就像顺便去家得宝买的一样。

sentences.en: Hey, it's five in the morning.
sentences.zh: 嘿，现在才早上五点。

sentences.en: I had an awful time getting these shovels this time of day, he says, and he lays them out.
sentences.zh: 他说道：“这大清早的，我费了好大劲才弄到这些铲子，”然后把它们摆放好。

sentences.en: There's a couple of reporters there taking notes.
sentences.zh: 有几个记者在那里做记录。

sentences.en: And the trustees dig in.
sentences.zh: 接着理事们开始铲土。

sentences.en: At least they try to.
sentences.zh: 至少他们试图这么做。

sentences.en: First off, you should note that it was in January in Chicago.
sentences.zh: 首先，你得知道那是芝加哥的1月。

sentences.en: So, you know, you don't shovel anything by hand.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，你根本没法用手铲土。

sentences.en: The ground was absolutely frozen and they were going absolutely nowhere.
sentences.zh: 地面完全冻结了，他们根本毫无进展。

sentences.en: So they bring in a dredge, which also goes nowhere.
sentences.zh: 于是他们调来一台疏浚机，结果同样毫无进展。

sentences.en: So they go get some dynamite.
sentences.zh: 所以他们去弄了些炸药。

sentences.en: Good old dynamite.
sentences.zh: 老牌好炸药。

sentences.en: Which is a dud.
sentences.zh: 结果是个哑炮。

sentences.en: It doesn't look very promising.
sentences.zh: 这看起来不太妙。

sentences.en: There was a lot of profanity.
sentences.zh: 现场爆出了许多粗口。

sentences.en: Number one, the trustees couldn't shovel it out.
sentences.zh: 第一，理事们根本铲不动。

sentences.en: And then the dynamite's not working.
sentences.zh: 然后炸药也不起作用。

sentences.en: And then the shovels aren't working.
sentences.zh: 接着铁锹也罢工了。

sentences.en: And, you know, this was like an insult to the kind of masculinity that we can't even, you know, open this thing up.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，这简直是一种对男子气概的侮辱，我们居然连这玩意儿都弄不开。

sentences.en: A couple hours later, it's like 10 in the morning now.
sentences.zh: 几个小时后，现在大约是早上10点。

sentences.en: And maybe 100 people have gathered.
sentences.zh: 大概聚集了一百人左右。

sentences.en: And the dredge gets to where it can just get one good scoop.
sentences.zh: 疏浚机终于开到了能够舀起漂亮一铲的地方。

sentences.en: And it grabs it.
sentences.zh: 它一把抓了下去。

sentences.en: Yeah, baby.
sentences.zh: 太棒了，宝贝。

sentences.en: A few more and a few more.
sentences.zh: 再来几铲，又来几铲。

sentences.en: And bam, everyone's shouting, it is open, it is open.
sentences.zh: 砰的一声，所有人都大喊起来，通了，通了。

sentences.en: Water starts dropping into the canal, 24 feet straight down.
sentences.zh: 水流开始落入运河，直落24英尺。

sentences.en: And away it goes.
sentences.zh: 水流奔涌而去。

sentences.en: It is the Niagara of Chicago, one of the trustees says.
sentences.zh: “这是芝加哥的尼亚加拉，”其中一位理事说道。

sentences.en: Almost there.
sentences.zh: 快大功告成了。

sentences.en: But there's still one last dam to open a bit down the river, which needed the governor's okay.
sentences.zh: 但河下游还剩最后一道水坝需要打开，这需要州长的批准。

sentences.en: It's a gate that's already been made.
sentences.zh: 这是一个已经造好的闸门。

sentences.en: So it's just a matter of turning the wheels that control the gate.
sentences.zh: 所以这只是转动控制闸门的轮子的事。

sentences.en: And once the gate was open, the water could not be stopped all the way down to New Orleans.
sentences.zh: 一旦闸门打开，水流就无法阻挡，一直流到新奥尔良。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, St. Louis is still gearing up its lawsuit.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，圣路易斯仍在加紧筹备诉讼。

sentences.en: They were always worried about St. Louis actually finding a lawsuit that would stop,
sentences.zh: 他们一直担心圣路易斯真的会提起诉讼来阻止，

sentences.en: that would enjoin them from actually opening the floodgates.
sentences.zh: 下达禁令阻止他们真正打开防洪闸。

sentences.en: And to this day, I can't figure out why St. Louis didn't do that.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，我也想不通为什么圣路易斯当时没有这么做。

sentences.en: Or why they were so slow about it.
sentences.zh: 或者为什么他们的动作那么慢。

sentences.en: But Chicago still had to jam a few last pieces into place to get the governor's okay.
sentences.zh: 但芝加哥仍然需要把最后几块拼图拼好才能获得州长的批准。

sentences.en: It took two weeks.
sentences.zh: 这花了两周时间。

sentences.en: St. Louis could have filed any day.
sentences.zh: 圣路易斯本可以在任何一天提起诉讼。

sentences.en: And then, January 17th, the trustees took one more early morning trek to lower the dam.
sentences.zh: 然后，在1月17日，理事们又进行了一次清晨远足去降低水坝。

sentences.en: They turned the crank, posed for a picture in their fancy coats and top hats,
sentences.zh: 他们转动曲柄，穿着华丽的大衣和高顶礼帽摆好姿势拍照，

sentences.en: then beat it back to Chicago for a big lunch.
sentences.zh: 随后赶回芝加哥享用了一顿丰盛的午餐。

sentences.en: While they were eating, they got word that St. Louis had indeed filed for an injunction that day.
sentences.zh: 正吃着饭，他们接到消息称，圣路易斯确实在当天提交了禁令申请。

sentences.en: Too late.
sentences.zh: 太迟了。

sentences.en: They brought a knife to a gunfight.
sentences.zh: 他们带了一把刀去参加枪战。

sentences.en: No, they brought a little piece of paper to a torrent of s**t fight.
sentences.zh: 不，他们带了一张纸去参加滔滔粪流之战。

sentences.en: Late, I might add.
sentences.zh: 而且还要我补充一句，太晚了。

sentences.en: They waited until just after the floodgates were open.
sentences.zh: 他们偏偏等防洪闸刚打开后才行动。

sentences.en: I can't understand that legal philosophy.
sentences.zh: 我真是无法理解那种法律哲学。

sentences.en: The story made the New York Times with the headline,
sentences.zh: 这个故事登上了《纽约时报》，头条是：

sentences.en: The water in the Chicago River now resembles liquid.
sentences.zh: 芝加哥河的水现在看起来像液体了。

sentences.en: St. Louis pushed their case to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 圣路易斯将案件推向了美国

sentences.en: Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 最高法院。

sentences.en: Chief Justice Oliver Wendell Holmes noted that,
sentences.zh: 首席大法官奥利弗·温德尔·霍姆斯指出：

sentences.en: It is a question of the first magnitude whether the destiny of the Great Rivers is to be the sewers of the cities along their banks.
sentences.zh: 大河的命运究竟是成为其沿岸城市的下水道，这是一个首要重大问题。

sentences.en: Which is an important philosophical question, but to paraphrase the way Justice Holmes finished that opinion,
sentences.zh: 这是一个重要的哲学问题，但用霍姆斯大法官结束该意见的方式来意译的话就是：

sentences.en: whatever, man.
sentences.zh: 管他呢，老兄。

sentences.en: Settling a question that big, it wasn't really the court's job,
sentences.zh: 解决这么大的问题，其实并不是法院的职责，

sentences.en: especially since Missouri allowed St. Louis and other towns to dump sewage into the Mississippi and send it straight to Memphis.
sentences.zh: 尤其是考虑到密苏里州允许圣路易斯和其他城镇将污水排入密西西比河并直接送往孟菲斯。

sentences.en: So, in a very real sense, there was no stopping it.
sentences.zh: 所以，从实际意义上讲，根本无法阻止。

sentences.en: The canal and river reversal was later called a civil engineering monument of the millennium.
sentences.zh: 运河和河流逆流工程后来被称为千禧年土木工程丰碑。

sentences.en: It was a functional monument to our dominion over the natural world.
sentences.zh: 它是我们统治自然世界的实用丰碑。

sentences.en: Or so we thought.
sentences.zh: 我们曾经是这么认为的。

sentences.en: Fast forward a hundred years to right about now,
sentences.zh: 快进一百年到现在的这个时候，

sentences.en: and the forces of nature are looking for another go-around.
sentences.zh: 大自然的力量正准备卷土重来。

sentences.en: There have been some big efforts to clean up the river itself in the last few decades.
sentences.zh: 在过去的几十年里，人们为清理这条河流本身做出了巨大的努力。

sentences.en: And by 2015, the treated sewage is actually supposed to get disinfected.
sentences.zh: 到2015年，处理后的污水实际上应该会被消毒。

sentences.en: And when Rich Cahan and I visited Bubbly Creek looking for bubbles,
sentences.zh: 当里奇·卡汉和我为了寻找气泡而参观泡泡溪时，

sentences.en: we may have seen signs of life there instead.
sentences.zh: 我们可能在那里看到了生命的迹象。

sentences.en: I see bubbles!
sentences.zh: 我看到气泡了！

sentences.en: Look!
sentences.zh: 看！

sentences.en: Look!
sentences.zh: 看！

sentences.en: I see those bubbles too.
sentences.zh: 我也看到那些气泡了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I think that's a fish, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我觉得那是条鱼，对吧？

sentences.en: See that?
sentences.zh: 看到那个了吗？

sentences.en: Right down there?
sentences.zh: 就在下面那里？

sentences.en: I definitely think it's some kind of living thing right there.
sentences.zh: 我绝对觉得那里某种活的生物。

sentences.en: Yes, yes, like a guppy.
sentences.zh: 对，对，就像孔雀鱼一样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: No, those are bubbles right there.
sentences.zh: 不，那些就是气泡。

sentences.en: Look at them.
sentences.zh: 看它们。

sentences.en: But now we're living in a time when the big 19th century interventions in nature
sentences.zh: 但现在我们生活的这个时代，19世纪对大自然的那些重大干预

sentences.en: seem poised to boomerang back at us.
sentences.zh: 似乎正准备对我们进行反噬。

sentences.en: Water levels in Lake Michigan have fallen, at least for now,
sentences.zh: 密歇根湖的水位已经下降了，至少目前是这样，

sentences.en: to the point where gravity may stop pulling lake water into the river,
sentences.zh: 下降到重力可能无法再把湖水拉入河中的程度，

sentences.en: potentially re-reversing the river,
sentences.zh: 这可能会让河流再次逆流，

sentences.en: if there weren't, you know, engineering interventions.
sentences.zh: 如果不是因为，你知道的，工程干预的话。

sentences.en: In terms of watching with Chicago's waste, it's mostly a symbolic issue.
sentences.zh: 就处理芝加哥的废弃物而言，这主要是一个象征性问题。

sentences.en: There are other ways to keep the water and treated sewage flowing away towards the Mississippi.
sentences.zh: 还有其他方法可以让水和处理后的污水继续流向密西西比河。

sentences.en: But falling lake levels, I mean, this is most of the fresh water in North America.
sentences.zh: 但湖水位下降，我的意思是，这可是北美大部分的淡水资源。

sentences.en: And a lot of people link this kind of falling lake levels to climate change
sentences.zh: 许多人把这种湖水位的下降与气候变化联系在一起，

sentences.en: and the whole catalog of horrors that comes with it.
sentences.zh: 以及与之相伴的一系列可怕灾难。

sentences.en: And it all seems like kind of a karmic payback
sentences.zh: 这一切看起来就像是一种因果报应，

sentences.en: for exactly the kinds of projects that reversing the Chicago River stood for.
sentences.zh: 正是对芝加哥河逆流这类工程项目的一种报应。

sentences.en: Or the idea that we can just do whatever we want to the planet and get away with it.
sentences.zh: 或者是那种认为我们可以对地球为所欲为却能逃脱惩罚的想法。

sentences.en: And I think that's a completely valid lesson you could take from this.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是你可以从中得出的一种完全合理的教训。

sentences.en: That the inherent hubris involved in reversing a river
sentences.zh: 那就是逆转一条河流所包含的与生俱来的傲慢，

sentences.en: or manipulating the environment to suit our needs
sentences.zh: 或者操纵环境以满足我们的需求，

sentences.en: is exactly what is wrong with us as stewards of this planet.
sentences.zh: 正是作为这个星球的管理者我们所犯的错误所在。

sentences.en: But taking another view,
sentences.zh: 但换个角度来看，

sentences.en: you could also see this as a lesson in the lengths we will go to survive.
sentences.zh: 你也可以把这看作是关于我们为了生存愿意付出多大努力的一课。

sentences.en: If we harness that 19th century moxie,
sentences.zh: 如果我们利用19世纪的那股冲劲，

sentences.en: the kind of moxie that makes you think that you could and should reverse a river,
sentences.zh: 那种让你觉得你可以而且应该逆转一条河流的冲劲，

sentences.en: and we add to that the knowledge we've gained since then,
sentences.zh: 再加上我们自那以后获得的知识，

sentences.en: we could guide our best and brightest to engineer the impossible,
sentences.zh: 我们就能引导我们最优秀、最聪明的人去设计出不可能实现的事情，

sentences.en: no matter what it takes.
sentences.zh: 无论付出什么代价。

sentences.en: And we would take day trips out to the far edge
sentences.zh: 我们会去远郊进行一日游，

sentences.en: and cheer them on as they save us from getting buried in our own s**t.
sentences.zh: 为他们加油呐喊，因为他们拯救了我们，让我们免于被自己的排泄物埋葬。

sentences.en: Or we could produce less s**t.
sentences.zh: 或者我们可以少产生点排泄物。

sentences.en: That'd be okay too.
sentences.zh: 那也挺好的。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Dan Weissman,
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%隐形》由丹·韦斯曼、

sentences.en: Sam Greenspan, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 萨姆·格林斯潘和我罗曼·马斯制作。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7,
sentences.zh: 我们是91.7节目组的一个项目，

sentences.en: local public radio, KALW in San Francisco,
sentences.zh: 即旧金山的本地公共广播电台KALW，

sentences.en: and the American Institute of Architects in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 以及旧金山美国建筑师学会。

sentences.en: You can find the show and like the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在Facebook上找到这个节目并点赞。

sentences.en: I tweet at Roman Mars right now.
sentences.zh: 我现在在Twitter上@Roman Mars。

sentences.en: Oh man, pictures of the Chicago River being reversed.
sentences.zh: 天哪，芝加哥河逆流的照片。

sentences.en: It's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: At 99%Invisible.org.
sentences.zh: 请访问99%Invisible.org。
